We build technology that empowers our drivers, transforms uncertainty into seamless flow, and sets the standard for real-time mobile navigation.
 We obsess over questions like: did your pickup spot feel safe and convenient? Did your driver feel confident following the route and arriving on the correct side of the road? ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F https://www.baseten.co/blog/announcing-our-series-f/, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.



THE ROLE

As a Site Reliability Engineer at Baseten, you'll define and codify the gold standards of day 2 operations for our ML infrastructure platform. You'll envision and build robust systems, processes, automations, and observability tooling that keep our platform reliable at scale — and that empower the broader organization to operate confidently.

You'll work closely with engineering, forward-deployed and product teams: learning from recurring failure patterns, turning tribal knowledge into automated mitigations, and raising the operational floor for the entire company.



EXAMPLE INITIATIVES

You'll work on projects like these as part of the SRE team:

 - Improve Baseten SRE Practices, by instrumenting SLOs and SLIs, improving alerting and observability for all services.

 - Building AI-assisted tooling for incident triage and response.
   
   

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the reliability of Baseten's multi-cloud Kubernetes infrastructure, including incident response, post-mortems, and remediation tracking.

 - Build and maintain observability infrastructure — metrics, logging, dashboards, and alerting — as code.

 - Author, validate, and improve runbooks for recurring failure patterns, ensuring they're structured for low-context, safe execution.

 - Identify high-frequency failure patterns and convert them into automated mitigations or self-healing automations.

 - Diagnose and resolve runtime issues related to latency, memory behavior, GPU utilization, concurrency, and model lifecycle management.

 - Define and instrument SLOs and SLIs across customer workloads and internal services.

 - Navigate ambiguity, make principled tradeoffs, and avoid unnecessary complexity in the systems you build and the processes you define.
   
   

REQUIREMENTS

 - Extensive hands-on experience with Kubernetes (multi-cloud experience across EKS, GKE, or similar is a strong plus).

 - Experience in building and maintaining scalable infrastructure.

 - Strong foundation in observability tooling: metrics (VictoriaMetrics, Prometheus), logging (Loki, ELK), dashboards (Grafana), and alerting pipelines. Observability-as-code experience is a plus.

 - Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Helm) and GitOps workflows (Flux CD, ArgoCD).

 - Experience writing and improving runbooks, leading incident response, and doing post-mortem analysis.

 - Comfort working at the intersection of engineering and operations — you write code, but you also think deeply about process, escalation paths, and operational leverage.

 - Familiarity with incident management platforms (incident.io http://incident.io or similar) is a plus.

 - No prior ML experience required, but curiosity about how ML models are deployed and served at scale will serve you well.



BENEFITS

 - Competitive compensation, including meaningful equity

 - (U.S. only) 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance for employee and dependents

 - Flexible PTO policy including company wide Winter Break (our offices are closed from Christmas Eve to New Year's Day!)

 - Paid parental leave

 - Fertility and family-building stipend through Carrot

 - (U.S. only) Company-facilitated 401(k)

 - Exposure to a variety of ML startups, offering unparalleled learning and networking opportunities.

Who are Tyk, and what do we do?  
 The Tyk API Management platform is helping to drive the connected world and power new products and services. We’re changing the way that organisations connect any number of their systems and services.Whether internal, external, public or highly encrypted systems, Tyk helps businesses drive value across the retail, finance, telecoms, healthcare, or media industries (to name just a few!)
 If you’ve banked online, used an app to check the news, or perhaps even driven a connected car, API’s, and by extension, Tyk, make that possible. Founded in 2015 with offices in London – UK, London – Ontario, Atlanta and Singapore, we have many thousands of users of our B2B platform across the globe. Brands using Tyk range from Lotte, Bell, T Mobile, to RBS, Capital One and Vinci. We have a varied user base hailing from every continent – even Antarctica.
 Our Mission
 Tyk is on a mission to connect every system in the world. We’ve started by building an API Management platform.
 Total flexibility, default remote, radical responsibility 
 We offer  unlimited paid holidays and remote working from anywhere in the world , for everyone, Why? Tyk was founded on the principle of offering flexibility and autonomy to our employees, we believe this allows our employees to achieve their best results. It also means we can build the best possible team, location and working hours are no barrier. 
 If this sounds like an environment that you believe could work for you then read on to find out more.
 The role:
 Tyk Cloud is our managed API management platform, running on multi-region Kubernetes at scale for customers around the world.
 We're looking for an SRE who's as comfortable in the code as in the infrastructure. You'll spend most of your time improving and automating the platform, and when you're on call, you'll handle incidents independently. You'll join a small, centralised SRE team that works closely with our product teams.
 You don't need to have done everything below. We care most about how you reason through problems and how quickly you learn. You'll have three to four months to get up to speed, shadowing first, before you go on call.
 What you'll do:
 Most of your time 
 Deliver the team's planned work each quarter, such as optimising the platform, building self-serve tooling for other teams, and rearchitecting parts of the platform as it grows.
 Help expand Tyk Cloud across regions and clouds, and bring down what it costs to run.
 Automate operations in Go, including building and maintaining our custom Kubernetes operators.
 Run the platform's services and databases, including MongoDB and Redis.
 Improve our observability: find the metrics that matter, and build the dashboards and alerts to act on them.
 Keep runbooks and documentation current, and support security work such as SOC 2 audits.
 When you're on call 
 You'll be doing one week in three initially (one in four as we grow), Monday-Friday, on a 12-hour shift with secondary backup support. Rotas: 14:00–02:00 UTC
 Be first line for platform alerts and incidents: restore service, escalate or help fix product bugs, and lead post-incident reviews.
 Act as second line for our Customer Success team, on requests that come directly from customers.

Legal Eagle? You get a strange amount of satisfaction from tightening a liability clause, spotting a hidden risk three sections deep, and finding a solution that protects the company without bringing business to a grinding halt. If you can turn complicated laws into practical advice, negotiate firmly without making enemies, and thrive in the fast-moving world of eCommerce, marketing, and consumer health, then you might have what it takes to join the legal team at AlgaeCal.
 Small Print ⇒ We’re looking for a commercially minded lawyer who can protect the business while helping it move forward. Someone who can review an influencer agreement in the morning, research a regulatory question before lunch, and calmly handle a demand letter in the afternoon without sending everyone around them into a panic.
 This job will give you ALL the feels:
 At AlgaeCal, we’re driven by a single idea. To end the fear of bone loss. In the United States, an estimated 54 million people have low bone density.
 The good news? AlgaeCal has the world’s only clinically supported natural solution to this problem. We give hope to everyone worried about bone loss. As our Junior Legal Counsel, you’ll help protect that trust. Your work will support responsible growth, compliant innovation, and the ethical decisions that allow us to reach more people without putting our customers, our brands, or our business at unnecessary risk.
 If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your legal career than at AlgaeCal. 
 This job might be for you if you… 
 Know your way around a contract. You know that the danger in a contract is rarely hiding in the font size. It’s buried in the indemnities, warranties, termination rights, intellectual property provisions, and limitations of liability. You’ve drafted and reviewed commercial agreements before, and you know how to identify the terms that truly matter for the business rather than drafting for academic rigour.
 Understand how business actually works. You don’t practise law in a vacuum. You understand that the goal isn’t simply to eliminate every imaginable risk. It’s to understand the risk, explain the trade-offs, and help the business make a smart decision. You can protect the company without becoming the Department of No. Instead, you’ll work within a team where our approach is How Can I Help. 
 Can make complicated things simple. You can take a complex legal issue and explain it in plain English to someone who has never set foot in law school. You write clear contracts, practical memos, useful summaries, and recommendations that help people understand what they need to do next.
 You know when to push back. You can challenge unreasonable terms without turning every negotiation into a courtroom drama. You know when to stand firm, when to compromise, and when a seemingly small clause creates a much bigger business risk.
 You spot problems early. You naturally notice the legal and compliance issues other people miss. Whether you’re reviewing marketing copy, packaging, a product name, a supplier agreement, or a new business initiative, you know how to identify potential exposure early and recommend a practical way to reduce it.
 You provide solutions. You take the time to understand what another business unit or leader is trying to achieve, uncover the problem behind the request, and bring them a practical solution. You research the options, explain the trade-offs, and set out a clear plan that protects the business while helping everyone get to the best possible outcome. 
 You care about protecting great brands. Trademarks, brand assets, product names, licensing, co-branding, and enforcement all interest you. You understand how valuable a strong brand can become, and you want to help protect it. And if you’ve got experience in intellectual property law, we’ll probably swoon.
 You’re comfortable in regulated territory. You understand that consumer health businesses operate in a complex regulatory environment. FDA, FTC, advertising law, privacy, disclaimers, licensing, and cross-border requirements don’t intimidate you. Experience in supplements, healthcare, eCommerce, or regulated consumer products would make us especially excited to meet you.
 You know when to keep your mouth shut. You’ll have access to sensitive business, employee, financial, and legal information. You treat that access to confidential information seriously. You exercise sound judgment, adhere to your professional obligations, and understand that discretion is not optional.
 You’ve already earned your legal stripes. You’ve completed a Juris Doctor, Bachelor of Laws, or equivalent qualification. You also bring one to two years of in-house legal experience or comparable commercial legal experience.
 You don’t let the little things slide. You’re obsessed with accuracy. You double-check your work, question inconsistencies, and take pride in delivering advice that people can trust.
 Now, time to be honest: is this really you? If you’re nodding your head and feeling that flutter of excitement, then we can’t wait to meet you. 
 Other Qualities You’ll Need 
 At AlgaeCal, we’re going to insist that you have these 3 qualities:
 You’re humble--you put the team and others’ needs ahead of your own
 You’re hungry to learn more
 You’re people smart--in the sense that you’re a great teammate
 The truth is, if you don’t have these qualities, you won’t last long at AlgaeCal. So if you’re missing one of them, be honest. Save yourself a lot of headaches and skip to a job posting that is a better fit for you.

 A generous healthcare package
 Monthly team events and activities
 Flexible Stat Holidays with the option to bank days for later use
 Weekly team lunches
 Casual dress code
 Incredible dog-friendly, Yaletown office one block from SkyTrain
 And above all, you’ll join a team that you’ll never want to leave. Culture is everything to us. Yes, we work extremely hard to change as many people’s lives as possible. But we know how to have fun and reward ourselves too.
 How To Apply

 Job opportunities like this don’t come along often, and we’ve got a lot to offer our successful applicant. So, to make sure our future Junior Legal Counsel is the real deal, will be a great fit, and will thrive at AlgaeCal, we ask a little more than your run-of-the-mill job application:

 Joignez-vous à l’équipe d’EDC! 
 À Exportation et développement Canada (EDC), nous aidons les entreprises canadiennes à réussir à l’étranger. Nous leur offrons les outils financiers et l’expertise dont elles ont besoin pour explorer de nouveaux marchés et réduire les risques, dans un seul but : bâtir un Canada et un monde meilleurs grâce au commerce. 
 Poste : Directrice ou directeur – Financement structuré et financement de projets, industries numériques et fabrication de pointe
 Type d’emploi : Permanent
 Détails de la rémunération : Directrice ou directeur, Souscription (niveau 22) Les salaires annuels varient généralement de 178 118 $ à 237 490 $, plus une rémunération au rendement, en fonction des qualifications et de l’expérience. 
 Lieu de travail : 
 EDC offre un modèle de travail hybride. Depuis septembre 2026, les employés doivent travailler au bureau trois jours par semaine; cette mesure est mise en œuvre progressivement en fonction de l’emplacement des employés (sous réserve de modifications). 
 La personne choisie devra travailler à partir du siège social d’EDC à Ottawa. Toutefois, les candidates et candidats situés à proximité de l’un des bureaux d’EDC à Toronto ou à Montréal seront également pris en considération.
 Une aide à la réinstallation à Ottawa est offerte aux candidates et candidats admissibles.
 Employés internes : veuillez consulter l’article de ServiceNow intitulé « Mouvements internes – Ce qu’il faut savoir ». 
 À propos d’EDC 
 À Exportation et développement Canada (EDC), nous aidons les entreprises canadiennes à réussir à l’étranger. Société d’État à vocation financière, EDC propose des solutions financières innovantes et des conseils d’experts pour aider les entreprises à explorer de nouveaux marchés, à atténuer leurs risques et à se développer.
 Pourquoi vous joindre à EDC? 
 Gamme complète d’avantages sociaux : EDC offre un régime de rémunération et d’avantages sociaux concurrentiel, une bonne conciliation travail-vie personnelle et la chance de contribuer à bâtir un Canada et un monde meilleurs grâce au commerce.
 Conciliation travail-vie personnelle : EDC offre un régime de rémunération concurrentiel et un équilibre travail-vie personnelle. Nous proposons des modalités de travail hybride, quatre semaines de vacances payées, une période de fermeture collective, des vendredis raccourcis en été et des vendredis sans réunion.
 Perfectionnement professionnel : Profitez de nos occasions d’apprentissage continu, notamment des programmes de formation, des ateliers et de la formation linguistique.
 Culture inclusive : Intégrez un milieu de travail diversifié et inclusif qui prône l’équité en matière d’emploi et valorise la diversité des idées, des forces et des origines pour favoriser la réussite.
 Programmes de bien-être : Nous offrons des initiatives de bien-être, de l’aide à la santé mentale et des programmes de conditionnement physique pour veiller à votre santé et à votre bonheur.
 Investissement dans la collectivité : Participez à des activités de bénévolat et donnez au suivant grâce à un éventail de programmes de responsabilité sociale.
 Aperçu de l’équipe et du poste 
Le Groupe du financement structuré et du financement de projets d’EDC, l’une des plus grandes équipes de financement de projets internationaux au Canada, joue un rôle important dans le financement de fusions et acquisitions, de projets et d’infrastructures à l’échelle mondiale. Depuis sa création en 1995, il a conclu plus de 700 transactions, qui totalisent plus de 60 milliards de dollars en financement. Au fil des années, le Groupe a bâti un portefeuille considérable touchant à différents secteurs, dont les suivants : mines et métaux, infrastructures, télécommunications, énergie, énergie renouvelable et technologies propres.
 Le financement structuré et le financement de projets constituent un domaine spécialisé des finances où les décisions sont prises en fonction des flux de trésorerie et des actifs propres à un projet donné. Les transactions sont généralement d’envergure et complexes. Les contreparties aux transactions appuyées par le Groupe du financement structuré et du financement de projets d’EDC comprennent des promoteurs canadiens et internationaux de premier rang, des exportateurs, des cabinets d’avocats ainsi que des banques de financement de projets et d’investissement internationales. 
 La directrice ou le directeur, Financement structuré et financement de projets est responsable du secteur des industries numériques et de la fabrication de pointe , ainsi que de la gestion d’une équipe composée de cinq à neuf professionnels. Il assure également l’orientation stratégique globale et la gestion opérationnelle d’équipes spécialisées en la matière. Les sous-secteurs relevant de la catégorie « Infrastructures » comprennent le numérique (télécommunications, centres de données, espace, etc.) et la fabrication de pointe, notamment dans les domaines de la défense et de la sécurité. La personne choisie démontrera des compétences de leadership avérées, de la flexibilité ainsi qu’un excellent sens de l’éthique professionnelle et misera sur les résultats.
 Ce que vous ferez: 
 Assurer la direction d’une équipe de spécialistes de produits.
 Incarner les grands principes de leadership d’EDC en veillant à instaurer une culture de rendement, de confiance et de réussite dans un esprit d’équipe.

 A day in the life (Responsibilities) 
 Run demos that win the room. Build every demo from discovery. Show a 40-site group their own menu, their own workflows and the systems they already run, in their market's version of the product. Tailor it to each person in the buying group, from the head of ops to the IT lead to finance. Leave each of them with a reason to champion Toast.
 Run labs that end in a decision. Agree success criteria with the customer before the lab starts. Build and maintain the lab environment, track every issue, drive escalations and root cause analysis, and close the lab with a clear yes or no. No lab ends without an agreed next step.
 Own the technical outcome through go-live. The deal isn't won until the customer is live and it matches what we sold. Stay involved through procurement and handoff.
 Architect the solution. Design how Toast fits into a multi-location group's existing stack:
 All of it within what's actually available, and what payments rules allow, in each market.
 Lead security, IT and compliance reviews. Own vendor security questionnaires, PCI scoping conversations and the technical sections of RFPs.
 Speak product's language. Write business requirement documentation that product and engineering can act on: the problem, the customer's own words, workarounds tried, what's at stake across the segment (not just one account), and options with tradeoffs. Turn one customer's ask into a case for the platform.

 Sell outcomes, not features. Partner with sales to build the business case. Translate technical fit into the outcomes the economic buyer cares about, such as labor, speed of service and revenue.  Engineer workarounds, and know when to hold the line. Design and document solutions to complex gaps, and judge when a workaround creates debt we'll pay for at go-live.
 Build real relationships outside the sales thread. Become the trusted counterpart to the customer's IT lead, head of operations and systems owners, relationships that hold up on their own merit.
 Hand off cleanly. Give onboarding and implementation a clear record of what was promised, what was configured and why, so delivery matches the sale.
 Help build the function. Set the engagement model for when and how AEs bring you in, qualify technical fit early and disqualify fast, and build reusable assets: demo environments for each market, reference architectures, an RFP library and BRD standards.
 Partner across Solutions. Work closely with the International SMB Solutions team on clear lanes, shared tools and cross-coverage.
 Grow the team. Help define, hire and develop the International upmarket solutions team as the business scales.
 Own your own leverage. Continuously find the repetitive parts of the role (RFP answers, security questionnaires, discovery notes, demo resets) and systematically get them off your plate.
 Close the loop on what's broken. Feed product gaps, lost-deal reasons and market differences back to product and sales leadership, so the next deal is easier than the last.

 You build and maintain your own environments. Demo data, lab configurations and resets are your job, done fast and adapted for each market.

 You've taken complex deals through lab or pilot to go-live. You can walk us through one end to end, including what went wrong and what you changed.

 Writing that product teams act on. Bring a sanitized requirements doc, solution design or BRD to the interview.
 Executive presence with C-suite and IT leaders, including delivering "no" and keeping the relationship.
 International experience across more than one market or regulatory regime. Willing to travel across the UK & Ireland, Canada and Australia (30%+).

 Hands-on experience with enterprise POS or hospitality platforms in these markets
 ERP, HR or workforce management integration experience
 MEDDPICC
